gen-dafont-capture-smallz-fs-synonym: Raw and chunky, all big-bodied lowercase. Synonym follows in sans-serif, one constant stroke width with generous curve openings, so the tactical heading gets a tidy, dependable partner underneath.
gen-dafont-capture-smallz-gf-lisu-bosa: Lisu Bosa sets sturdy, tall serif lowercase. Capture Smallz is blunt and raw while the serif body flexes gently like spring wire, and that shift from abrupt to gradual is the pair's best trick.
gen-dafont-cargo-work-sans: Cargo's glyphs sit loose and nearly closed, striking and raw. Work Sans is sans-serif with round-pen openness, so if Cargo were made small, its tight c would clog while the body stays clear.
gen-dafont-cheri-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Cheri is cute, calligraphic and sturdy, with no hairlines at all. Be Vietnam Pro sans-serif body keeps its bent-rod strokes and distant curve endings, so a longer passage would move along cleanly beneath it.
gen-dafont-cheri-fs-familjen-grotesk: Familjen Grotesk, a plain sans with unfinished bowls and tall lowercase, brings lively energy beneath the script heading. Cheri's curves carry no stress, so next to it the pair feels friendly but a bit playful, comfortable in small doses.
gen-dafont-cheri-fs-fira-sans: Friendly script, sturdy and calligraphic, from Cheri. Fira Sans, a plain sans with no thick and thin contrast and a generous x-height, would carry a longer passage with steady, open readability.
gen-dafont-cheri-fs-ranade: Ranade reads organic and spacious, with stroke ends set far apart and only a slight weight shift. Cheri's pipe-like script strokes meet its light, pressed-glass swells, and that tension between tubular and gently swollen is what makes the pair work.
gen-dafont-chinese-rocks-fs-karma: Striking, wiry letters cut tight together make up Chinese Rocks. And Karma, a serif with terminals well clear of the stem and a smooth narrowing from stem to tip, would read steadily over a longer stretch.
gen-dafont-chrome-fs-supreme: Supreme reads crisp, with a heavy middle band and letters held open. Chrome is the one to deliver weight, post-like stems collapsing to wire curves, while Supreme's strength is plain, open clarity.
gen-dafont-college-fs-erode: Erode reads dignified, with a tall middle band and gently ebbing weight. College does the loud work with thick, uniform curves and big counters; Erode, the serif, does the quiet editorial work.
